For RGAA test 2.1.1. Elements: every <iframe> and <frame> element in the top document and in every document nested in it through frames, shadow trees included. If any nested document cannot be read, answer cannot_tell for the page. For each frame element, in this order: (1) it has a title attribute whose value contains a non-whitespace character: the requirement holds for it. (2) It has a title attribute that is empty or only whitespace: cannot_tell (the wording asks for the attribute; the glossary defines the frame title as its content). (3) It has no title attribute and aria-hidden="true" is set on it, on an ancestor in its document, or on a frame element that hosts that document: cannot_tell, since the exception for technical frames hidden with aria-hidden may apply and deciding it needs judgment. (4) It has no title attribute and is not rendered (computed display none on it or an ancestor, computed visibility hidden or collapse, or inside a frame that is itself not rendered): cannot_tell. (5) Otherwise: fault on that element. The check ignores aria-label, aria-labelledby and role, which the test does not accept in place of title. Page result: fault if any frame falls under (5); otherwise cannot_tell if any falls under (2), (3) or (4); otherwise no_fault if there is at least one frame; inapplicable if there is no frame element at all.

For RGAA test 6.2.1. Elements: in the top document and every document nested in it through frames, shadow trees included, every HTML element with an href attribute, every SVG element with an href or xlink:href attribute, and every element with an explicit role="link". An without href or xlink:href is an anchor and is skipped (technical note of criterion 6.2). If a nested document cannot be read, answer cannot_tell for the page. For each element, compute its name from content only, ignoring aria-labelledby, aria-label, title and xlink:title on the element itself: walk its descendants, skip every subtree that is hidden from assistive technologies (aria-hidden="true", computed display none, computed visibility hidden or collapse, the hidden attribute), and collect: the data of text nodes; for an or an element with role img or image, its text alternative from aria-labelledby, then aria-label, then alt, then title; for an inline

For RGAA test 7.3.2. Evidence only. Runs in the keyboard pass. Elements: every element that receives focus while the Tab key moves through the page's sequential focus order, in the top document, shadow trees included, and in nested frame documents that can be read. For each one: record the deep active element (through shadow roots and readable frames) right after the key press; then wait 500 ms with no input and read it again. Fault on the element when focus is now on the document body or on no element, while the element is still connected, rendered, not disabled, not inert and still focusable: its focus was removed without user action. cannot_tell for the element when focus has moved to another element or into a frame, or when the element was removed, hidden, disabled or made inert meanwhile (whether these count as removing focus is not decided here). Elements that can take focus only from a pointer are not examined, and the particular case of criterion 7.3 is not examined. Page result: fault if any element has a fault; otherwise cannot_tell if any element is cannot_tell or the pass did not complete; otherwise no_fault; inapplicable when no element receives focus.

For RGAA test 7.3.1. Evidence only. Elements: in the top document, shadow trees included, every element with an event listener attached directly to it for click, dblclick, mousedown, mouseup, pointerdown, pointerup, touchstart, touchend, keydown, keyup or keypress, read through the DevTools protocol (DOMDebugger.getEventListeners, which includes on* attributes). Fault on such an element when it is rendered, not disabled, not inert, not in the sequential focus order (not natively focusable and without tabindex, or with a negative tabindex), and has no ancestor that is in the sequential focus order. cannot_tell for such an element when an ancestor is in the sequential focus order (keyboard activation of the ancestor may perform the same action). Listeners attached to window, document, html or body cannot be attributed to elements: when any of the event types above is listened for there, the page result is cannot_tell unless a fault exists. A fault says only that Tab cannot reach the element; it says nothing about an equivalent element elsewhere in the page, keyboard shortcuts, pointer access, or the particular case of criterion 7.3. Page result: fault if any element has a fault; otherwise cannot_tell as above; otherwise no_fault; inapplicable when no element has such a listener.

For RGAA test 8.3.1. Scope: the top-level document of the page (documents in frames are not part of it). Document type: XHTML 1.1 when the doctype public identifier contains "XHTML 1.1"; XHTML 1.0 when it contains "XHTML 1.0", split by the served content type (document.contentType) into text/html and application/xhtml+xml; other XML when it contains "XHTML" otherwise or the document is served as application/xhtml+xml without one of those doctypes; otherwise HTML. Indication required on an element: HTML: lang; XHTML 1.0 as text/html: lang and xml:lang; XHTML 1.0 as application/xhtml+xml: xml:lang; XHTML 1.1: xml:lang; other XML: lang and xml:lang. xml:lang is read with getAttributeNS("http://www.w3.org/XML/1998/namespace", "lang") in XML documents and as the attribute named xml:lang in text/html documents. An element carries the indication when every required attribute is present with a value holding a non-whitespace character. Text items: every text node with a non-whitespace character, except inside script, style, template and noscript, plus every element with a non-whitespace alt, title, aria-label or placeholder attribute, or the value of an input of type button, submit or reset. The language source of a text item is its nearest inclusive ancestor that has a lang or xml:lang attribute in any form, walking up through shadow hosts. Answer, in this order: (1) the html element carries the indication: no_fault. (2) At least one text item exists and every text item's language source carries the indication: no_fault. (3) The html element has a lang or xml:lang attribute in any form, even empty or not the one the type requires: cannot_tell. (4) Some text item inside body has no language source at all and is rendered (a text node with a non-empty client rect and computed visibility visible, or an element with a layout box) or is exposed in the accessibility tree: fault, reported on that item. (5) Otherwise (no text item, only items outside body uncovered such as the title, only unrendered items uncovered, or items whose language source has an empty or unsuitable attribute): cannot_tell. Never inapplicable.

For RGAA test 8.4.1, the validity condition only (relevance is not examined). Scope: the html element of the top-level document, with the document types, required attributes and way of reading xml:lang defined for custom/8-3-default-lang-present. For each required attribute present on the html element: if its value is empty or has leading or trailing whitespace, cannot_tell for it. Otherwise take the part of the value before the first hyphen (the whole value if there is none) and compare it, ignoring ASCII case, with a pinned list holding every ISO 639-1 code, every ISO 639-2 code in both its bibliographic and terminologic forms (including the reserved range qaa to qtz and the codes mis, mul, und and zxx), every ISO 639-3 code and every ISO 639-5 code, plus codes since deprecated or withdrawn from any of those parts (such as iw, in, ji, mo); record the list's version with the check. Fault on the attribute when that part is not in the list. When the html element has none of the required attributes, answer cannot_tell: the default language may be given on each text element instead, which this check does not examine, or be missing, which is for 8.3.1. Attributes on html that the document type does not require are not examined. Page result: fault if any required attribute has a fault; no_fault when every required attribute is present and its code is in the list; otherwise cannot_tell. Never inapplicable.
